items.title: NEW — a `css { … }` block is `const` BY CONSTRUCTION: today `let b = css { padding: 1rem; };` is refused ("`raw` … is compile-time-only; evaluate this call inside a `const` expression") and every block needs `const` written in front; a block is a compile-time asset by definition, so it is one, and const-eval refuses a hole that reads a runtime value
items.discussion: the owner's sketch (2026-09-07: `css { // auto const`); probed on a5473227
items.body: The css desugaring wraps its chain in `const`; a hole reading a runtime binding gets const-eval's existing refusal at the hole. Pins: `let b = css {…}` compiles; `.styled(css {…})` on an element compiles; a runtime hole is refused at the hole; the written `const css {…}` still compiles (idempotent).

items.title: NEW — a CHAIN LINK inside a `css` block: a dotted item ending in `;` (`.ghost();`, `.flex_row();`, `.custom_method(a, b);`) is a verbatim `Style` method call in written position, while a dotted item with a block stays a condition rule — the element syntax's own rule (dotted = chain link), and the way an app's helpers and std's combinators reach the block
items.discussion: the owner's sketch (`.custom_method()` inside the block, 2026-09-07); css-block.md §10 refused "composing styles inside a block" and left the grammar space free — this is the ask that wants it
items.body: Grammar: `css-item = declaration | condition-rule | chain-link`, `chain-link = "." name ["(" args ")"] ";"`; lowering: the link is emitted at its written position in the chain (the chain sorter's canonical order applies afterwards as to any chain). Pins: a bare link, a link with arguments, a link between declarations, the condition rule untouched; formatter round-trip; kolt's `flex_row`/`ghost`/`select_off` helpers as the read-only exhibit.

items.title: NEW — `std::style::prelude`: free-function aliases of the typed tokens (`rem`, `px`, `em`, `pct`, `vh`, `vw`, `auto`, `space`; `black`, `white`, `transparent`, `hex`, `gray`, `blue`, `red`, `green`, `rgba`, `oklch`; `s()` for `style()`), AMBIENT inside css-block holes (names.md's ambient-module precedent) and importable in any block — so `{rem(4)}` and `{red(500)}` are the hole spellings and `const { import std::style::prelude; s().p(…) }` is a legal local scope
items.discussion: the owner's two sketches (2026-09-07); block-scoped imports have shipped since July, `const { … }` works as a block expression — the prelude module is the only missing piece for both
items.body: One module of one-line delegations; the css lowering resolves hole names against it first (an explicit local binding still wins); the `style` chain untouched. Pins: a hole prelude name, a local binding shadowing it, the block-import form, and the three kolt styles converted in a scratch copy with character counts before/after.

items.title: NEW — css-block editor smalls: `:hover {` inside a block is refused with the bare `found ':' expected a declaration …` where a STEER to `.hover { … }` is owed (the dotted rule is deliberate — one name-blind rule covers pseudo-classes, breakpoints, `within`, `divide`); and PROPERTY-NAME completion inside a block from the closed CSS property list (values stay token runs — css-block.md §10's non-goal is value completion, not names)
items.discussion: the owner tried `:hover` (2026-09-07); property names are the "write" half of compact styling
items.body: Ledger row EDIT for the `:` case (a steer naming `.hover`), a completion source of CSS property names (a generated list, versioned with std) offered at declaration position inside a block; pins for both.
